memory_candidates.content: When capturing bash command exit code alongside stdout in a subshell assignment, `output=$(cmd 2>&1) || true; exit_code=$?` always returns 0 for exit_code because `$?` captures the exit of `|| true`. Use a temp file instead: `cmd > tmpout 2>&1; exit_code=$?; output=$(cat tmpout); rm tmpout`.

Routing values in extension manifests may use colon sub-operation suffixes (e.g., `skill-grant:assemble`). When validating routing targets against provides.skills or the deployed tree, strip the suffix with `${target%%:*}` to get the base skill name. Failure to do this causes false-positive FAILs from the present extension's compound routing values.
